items.title: 1980 Harvey's Casino Bombing
items.channel_title: The History Guy: History Deserves to Be Remembered
items.description:
On August 26, 1980, some men wearing jumpsuits drove up in a white Dodge van and rolled a large box into a Casino  in Stateline Nevada, saying that they were delivering a copy machine. It wasn’t a copy machine. Thus began what the Federal Bureau of Investigation described as “one of the most unusual cases” in the bureau’s history.

items.why_watch: In 1980, a man smuggled a 1,000-pound bomb into Harvey's Casino disguised as a copy machine — then sent a ransom note demanding $3 million and daring the FBI to disarm it. The History Guy walks through the remarkably specific engineering of the device and the FBI's agonizing decision about how to respond. It's a genuinely strange true-crime story that somehow never became a household name.

In this video I'll talk about a Zettelkasten note-taking system, invented by Niklas Luhmann and why it works, so that you can take inspiration from these principles and incorporate them into your o
items.why_watch: A Harvard neuroscience PhD student explains Zettelkasten not as a productivity hack but through the lens of how the brain actually forms and connects ideas — which gives the system's design choices real logical weight. In 12 minutes, you'll understand why the method's insistence on atomic, linked notes isn't arbitrary, and you'll leave with a clear mental model for whether it fits how you actually think and work.

discovery_articles.title: Jolly's Mill Pond in Williamsburg, Virginia
discovery_articles.snippet: On a quiet stretch of water just outside Williamsburg, recipes, archives, and heirloom crops are revealing stories that conventional history has overlooked. Dating back to the late 18th century, Jolly’s Mill Pond has become an outdoor classroom where Black, Indigenous, agricultural, and culinary histories are explored together around a shared table. In the late 1700s, the pond and its dam were created to power a gristmill that served the surrounding community.

garden_note.note: August's last full moon hangs heavy and golden over the Zürichsee tonight, the kind of light that makes the kitchen garden look almost theatrical — dahlias casting long shadows, runner beans glowing at their tips.
